prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the Conservative Party Manifesto 1997 (under 500 words)

Vision and record
- Build on post‑1979 reforms to keep Britain the best place to live: a low‑tax, enterprise economy; strong public services; safe communities; national unity; a sovereign role in Europe.
- Highlighted record: faster growth than major EU economies, lowest EU tax burden among majors, falling unemployment, low inflation and mortgage rates, inward investment leadership, privatisation-driven service improvements.

Economy, jobs, business
- Keep public spending below 40% of GDP; move toward a balanced budget by 2000; maintain 2.5% inflation target; aim for a 20p basic income tax rate (top rate capped at 40p).
- Preserve the UK’s low-cost, flexible labour market: reject EU Social Chapter, Working Time Directive and a national minimum wage; resist new EU employment burdens.
- Help small firms: cut small companies’ corporation tax toward 20p; reform business rates to favour small businesses; reduce capital taxes prudently; sunset and slim regulations; tackle late payment; extend competition law (new Competition Bill).
- Welfare to work: extend Project Work nationwide; strengthen Jobseeker’s Allowance conditionality; launch “Britain Works” with private/voluntary partners.
- Information society and science: “IT for All,” connect schools; use Millennium Fund for public IT access; efficient spectrum pricing; maintain free, competitive media; target basic research.

Families, ownership, pensions, social care
- Prioritise family tax relief: allow transfer of unused personal allowance to a working spouse where caring for dependent children/relatives (worth up to £17.50/week).
- Promote savings and ownership: expand employee share schemes (Share Match), develop PEP/TESSA-style reliefs, raise inheritance thresholds prudently.
- Pensions reform: for new entrants, create funded personal pension accounts via NI rebates with a state guarantee at least equal to the current basic pension; more flexibility for AVCs and job moves.
- Social Services Reform Bill: clearer accountability and standards across public/private providers; expand direct payments/vouchers; national Respite Care Programme; partnership funding for long‑term care; streamline adoption; uphold Disability Discrimination Act.

Education and skills
- Education Guarantee: national targets; testing at 5, 7, 11, 14; publish results; rigorous basics (phonics, arithmetic without calculators), strong A‑levels; tighter teacher appraisal; more discipline powers; religious education and worship upheld.
- Choice and diversity: expand grant‑maintained status and school self‑governance; allow selection by aptitude; more specialist schools; enable grammar schools where parents want; expand Assisted Places; maintain universal nursery vouchers.
- Lifetime learning: learning credits (14–21), National Traineeships, more rigorous NVQs; respond to Dearing on HE.

Health and public services
- NHS: real-terms funding rises each year; expand medical and specialist nursing staff; publish clinical outcomes; extend GP fundholding and primary care services; nurses’ prescribing; strengthen mental health services; prevention via Health of the Nation; modernise infrastructure through PFI.
- Public service reform: Citizen’s Charter expansion; “government direct” digital services; extend competition and privatisation where beneficial (Parcelforce, NATS; consider Royal Mail private capital while preserving universal service); privatise London Underground with fare caps; complete rail privatisation; roads via PFI; curb disruptive strikes in essential services.

Law, order, drugs
- More police and CCTV; tackle petty and youth crime: Parental Control Orders, speedy sanctions with reparation, pilot juvenile curfews; create a National Crime Squad.
- Sentencing: mandatory life for a second serious violent/sexual offence; minimums for persistent burglars (3 years) and hard‑drug dealers (7 years); end automatic early release; strengthen victims’ protections; speed up justice; tougher on City fraud; comprehensive anti‑drugs strategy.

Environment, cities, rural, agriculture
- Regenerate worst estates via £25bn private investment through voluntary housing transfers; reduce empty public homes; continue Rough Sleepers Initiative.
- Protect green belt; target >60% new homes on brownfield; support rural shops/post offices and rural enterprise; managed access, not a general right to roam; lead on animal welfare.
- Agriculture: robust BSE response; independent Chief Food Safety Adviser; reform CAP; defend fisheries (quota hopping, inshore limits).

Europe, constitution, defence, world
- Europe as a partnership of nation states: keep veto, borders, rebate; no federalism or Social Chapter; flexible union; complete single market; reform ECJ; enlargement.
- Single currency: unlikely safe in 1999; keep options open; any entry only after a national referendum.
- Defence: NATO cornerstone; no defence review; maintain Trident; invest in rapid deployment and technology; support reserves and cadets.
- Constitution: evolutionary reform, more openness; oppose devolution to Scottish/Welsh assemblies and PR; maintain Union; NI talks with consent, firm against terror.
- Global role: UN reform, peacekeeping, NATO/EU enlargement, Commonwealth, targeted aid, climate leadership.
